title: incident-bot: on-call autodiagnostics - priority sampling heuristic + SLO hints
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: on-call autodiagnostics currently surface a large number of candidate runbooks and SLOs which makes triage noisy during high-volume incidents. This PR introduces a priority sampling heuristic used by incident-bot and complementary SLO hint generation in slo-toolkit to surface higher-signal items to on-call responders.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a lightweight priority sampler that weights runbook/SLO candidates by recent error impact, owner response latency, and historical correctness (incident-to-runbook hit rate). 2) Emits a compact SLO hint payload that ranks SLOs and annotates likely causal signals for autodiagnostics. 3) Integrates the sampler into the on-call autodiagnostics pipeline with an opt-in feature flag. 4) Adds end-to-end unit and integration tests and updates the runbook linking docs.

Key design notes: - Sampler is conservative: it uses sampling windows and decay factors to avoid oscillation during noisy bursts. - Heuristics are pluggable; future work will allow ML-based ranking. - SLO hints are intentionally small (<=1KB) to keep the diagnostic messages lightweight for chat and Slack integrations.

Checklist: - [x] New priority_sampler module + tests - [x] SLO hint schema and generator - [x] Integration wiring behind feature flag - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Docs: runbook linking and configuration example - [x] Changelog/release notes entry

Related: ENG-4021 (on-call quality improvements), ENG-4080 (slo-toolkit hinting).
